intent: To illustrate that individuals who do not attend college are concentrated in lower income brackets, supporting the argument that post-secondary training is economically necessary and student debt cancellation is irrelevant for this group.

requirements.question: Must the clip show the full downward trend, or is a single high-low endpoint contrast sufficient?
Is the low-end group comparison required, or is the overall non-college downward trend enough?
Is the top-end gap required to reinforce that non-college individuals are not concentrated in high brackets?

units.claim: The DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE series is highest in the lowest income bracket and decreases monotonically across the income brackets, reaching its lowest value in the highest income bracket.

basis.note: highest non-college relative_value; lowest income bracket
lowest non-college relative_value; highest income bracket

accept: Non-college attendance peaks in the lowest income bracket and falls as income rises.
The DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE segment is most concentrated at the bottom of the income distribution and least at the top.
The non-college series slopes downward from the lowest bracket to the highest bracket.
units.evidence: The values for DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE must be shown descending from the lowest-income category to the highest-income category.

units.claim: In the lowest two income brackets, the DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE relative value is larger than the ATTENDED COLLEGE relative value.
accept: The non-college group is the larger group in the bottom two income brackets.
At the low end, DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE exceeds ATTENDED COLLEGE.
The non-college value is about three times the college-attended value in the lowest bracket.
units.evidence: In the lowest two income categories, the DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE value must appear greater than the ATTENDED COLLEGE value.

units.claim: In the highest income bracket, the ATTENDED COLLEGE relative value is much larger than the DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE relative value; the gap is 0.55 minus 0.05.
accept: At the top income bracket, the college-attended group is far larger than the non-college group.
The non-college segment is smallest at the top, far below the college-attended segment.
The widest top-end gap between the two groups is in the highest income bracket.
units.evidence: In the highest income category, the ATTENDED COLLEGE value must appear much greater than the DIDN'T ATTEND COLLEGE value.

optional_valid: The middle-bracket equality at 0.50 can be omitted if the clip focuses only on the low-end concentration and top-end gap.
The plateau of ATTENDED COLLEGE in the top two brackets is optional detail.
The exact ordering of the ATTENDED COLLEGE values between the upper-middle and top brackets can be simplified if the main contrast is preserved.

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

clip_hardcase.reason: The reference SVG has no explicit data-role=bar mark, so visual-unit reconstruction needs manual review.

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
